#: has not been delimited scan-by-scan the way the Czech one has — so this is the
#: *estimate* used for pricing only, and a DE run is given explicit pages. It is
#: named rather than inlined so that a wrong number is visible rather than buried
#: in an arithmetic expression.
DE_PAGE_COUNT_ESTIMATE = 490

#: Printed, unmistakably a symbol, and absent from the curated list. Distinct
#: from `[?]` (printed, illegible): `[?]` is a limit of the reading, `[!]` is a
#: limit of the atlas, and only the second one is a to-do.
NOT_IN_ATLAS = "[!]"

#: The five development pages. They sit **outside both halves of the gold sample**
#: by design (``draw_gold_sample.ALREADY_READ``), so reading them changes nothing
#: about the draw or its confidence interval.
PURPOSIVE_PAGES = (118, 270, 449, 450, 451)

#: The pages ``inventory_human.csv`` covers — the hand-read claims every accuracy
#: number in this project is measured against: 280 over 47 entries from the first
#: reading, 372 over 61 since the gold became the whole-page sheets (D-65).
GOLD_SCORED_PAGES = (118, 270, 450, 451)

#: The one purposive page that is transcribed in the whole-page format **and** is
#: absent from :data:`GOLD_SCORED_PAGES`. That makes it the only page that can be
#: used as a few-shot example without grading a model against its own prompt —
#: the rule D-38 already enforces on the readers. Never few-shot from a
#: calibration or certification page: a page spent as a prompt is spent as
#: evaluation data.
FEWSHOT_PAGE = 449


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Image rules — how each provider turns pixels into tokens
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# This is the part that decides both the bill and what the model can actually see,
# and the two providers are not close to each other. It lives on the model spec so
# the tiler is model-aware without a single branch at the call site.


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ImageRule:
    """How one provider bills and resizes an image.

    ``max_edge`` / ``max_px`` are the thresholds **above which the provider
    downscales**. A rule that tiles (``tiles=True``) cuts the page so no tile
    crosses them, which is the whole point: an image that gets downscaled loses
    exactly the pictograms this volume is being read for.

    ``tokens(w, h)`` is the provider's own accounting for one image already inside
    those bounds. It is used for the pre-flight estimate only — every real call
    reports its usage and the ledger overrides this.
    """

    name: str
    tiles: bool
    max_edge: int
    max_px: int
    tokens: Callable[[int, int], int]
    note: str = ""


def _anthropic_tokens(width: int, height: int) -> int:
    """``w × h / 750``, the documented Anthropic image-token formula."""
    return math.ceil(width * height / 750)


def _gemini_tokens(width: int, height: int) -> int:
    """768 × 768 crops at 258 tokens each — Gemini's own tiling, done server-side.

    This is why Gemini needs no pre-tiling: it takes the full-resolution page and
    crops it itself, at roughly a third of the tokens Anthropic charges for the
    same pixels. ⚠ Verify with ``client.models.count_tokens`` before trusting it
    for a volume estimate — :func:`token_reality_check` does exactly that.
    """
    return math.ceil(width / 768) * math.ceil(height / 768) * 258


#: Anthropic: long edge 1568 px, ~1.15 Mpx an image. A 2,714 × 3,976 page needs
#: ten tiles to stay native.
LONG_EDGE_1568 = ImageRule(
    name="long-edge-1568", tiles=True, max_edge=1568, max_px=1_150_000,
    tokens=_anthropic_tokens,
    note="tiles the page to keep native resolution; ~18k tokens/page")

#: Gemini: hand it the page whole. Its own 768 px crops preserve the resolution
#: and cost about a third as much.
CROP_768_258 = ImageRule(
    name="crop-768-258", tiles=False, max_edge=0, max_px=0,
    tokens=_gemini_tokens,
    note="page sent whole at native resolution; ~6k tokens/page")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The model registry
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelSpec:
    """Everything that differs between one model and another, in one place.

    A registry rather than a chain of ``if provider == …``: adding a model is one
    entry, and every part of the pipeline that needs to know something
    model-specific — the tiler, the estimator, the adapter, the ledger — reads it
    from here instead of re-deriving it from the model id. Deriving behaviour from
    an id string is how v1's ``OCR_MODEL_MARKS`` heuristic came to guess a prompt
    style from a substring.
    """

    key: str
    provider: str
    model_id: str
    price_in: float                 # USD per million input tokens, standard rate
    price_out: float                # USD per million output tokens, standard rate
    image_rule: ImageRule
    batch_discount: float = 0.5
    thinking: str | None = "off"    # "off" | None (provider default) | effort name
    max_output_tokens: int = 32_000
    price_note: str = ""
    #: Environment variables this provider's SDK reads, in the order it tries
    #: them. On the registry rather than in the adapter so that
    #: :func:`credentials_report` can say what is missing *before* a run starts,
    #: instead of the SDK raising an auth error twenty minutes into a batch.
    key_env: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    #: Largest batch this provider will accept, in bytes of wire payload.
    #:
    #: Anthropic documents 256 MB for the Message Batches API and refuses the
    #: whole submission with a 413 — not a partial accept — so the margin here is
    #: deliberate. Google's inline ceiling is not documented in the same place;
    #: 180 MB is set below the ~200 MB an earlier run was observed to accept
    #: rather than above it.
    max_batch_bytes: int = 200_000_000
    #: Sampling temperature, or **None to send none at all**.
    #:
    #: Not a uniform setting, which is exactly why it lives here. Gemini and
    #: Haiku 4.5 accept it; **Claude Sonnet 5 rejects it with a 400** — sampling
    #: parameters were removed on that model generation — so its entry carries
    #: None and the adapter omits the field rather than the run discovering this
    #: one page into a batch.
    #:
    #: 0.0 is the default but not obviously right, and the pilot cannot say:
    #: nothing was sent, so both providers ran at their own defaults. Greedy
    #: decoding can lock into repetition over the ~13k tokens of JSON a page
    #: costs, and it forfeits repeat sampling as a recall lever. Reproducibility
    #: is *not* the argument for it — that comes from the archived payloads under
    #: `raw/<run_id>/`, not from the sampler, and no provider here guarantees
    #: determinism anyway. Sweep it on the gold pages and keep what reads best.
    temperature: float | None = 0.0


MODELS: dict[str, ModelSpec] = {
    # Priced 2026-09-08. The $0.75/$3.75 is an *introductory* rate that expires
    # 2026-12-31 and doubles on 2027-01-01 — which takes the full CZ+DE run from
    # $32 to $64. Four months of runway, and it is the reason to run the volume
    # this year rather than next.
    "gemini-3.8-flash": ModelSpec(
        key="gemini-3.8-flash", provider="google", model_id="gemini-3.8-flash",
        price_in=0.75, price_out=3.75, image_rule=CROP_768_258,
        thinking="off", price_note="intro rate; doubles 2027-01-01",
        key_env=("GEMINI_API_KEY", "GOOGLE_API_KEY"),
        max_batch_bytes=180_000_000),
    "claude-haiku-4-5": ModelSpec(
        key="claude-haiku-4-5", provider="anthropic", model_id="claude-haiku-4-5",
        price_in=1.00, price_out=5.00, image_rule=LONG_EDGE_1568,
        thinking="off", key_env=("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",)),
    "claude-sonnet-5": ModelSpec(
        key="claude-sonnet-5", provider="anthropic", model_id="claude-sonnet-5",
        price_in=2.00, price_out=10.00, image_rule=LONG_EDGE_1568,
        thinking="off", key_env=("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",),
        # Sampling parameters were removed on this model generation: sending
        # temperature/top_p/top_k returns a 400. None means "omit the field".
        temperature=None),
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Credentials
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# `notebooks/*.ipynb` is **tracked**. A key pasted into a cell is committed, and a
# key in git history is not removed by deleting the line — it is removed by
# rewriting history, which nobody does. The repo being private does not change
# that: a private repo can be forked, cloned to a second machine, or shared with
# a co-author, and the key travels with it.
#
# So keys never enter the notebook source. They come from the environment, or
# from a gitignored file next to the repo, and the notebook's own cell prompts
# for them without echoing.

#: Where a saved key file lives. Gitignored as a directory, so a key cannot be
#: added to it later under a different filename and be committed by accident.
SECRETS_DIR = ROOT / ".secrets"
KEY_FILE = SECRETS_DIR / "api_keys.json"

#: Also read, because it is the convention most tooling already expects and the
#: user may already have one.
DOTENV = ROOT / ".env"


def load_credentials(verbose: bool = False) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Put saved API keys into ``os.environ``, and say where each came from.

    Resolution order, first hit wins per variable:

    1. an already-set environment variable — so an externally managed key,
       a CI secret or ``ant auth login`` is never overwritten by a stale file;
    2. :data:`KEY_FILE` (JSON);
    3. :data:`DOTENV` (``NAME=value`` lines).

    Returns ``{variable: source}``. It never returns or prints a key value.
    """
    import os

    found: dict[str, str] = {}
    for var in _all_key_vars():
        if os.environ.get(var):
            found[var] = "environment"

    for path, reader in ((KEY_FILE, _read_json_keys), (DOTENV, _read_dotenv)):
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        try:
            saved = reader(path)
        except Exception as exc:                        # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  ! {path.name} unreadable ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for var, value in saved.items():
            if var in found or not value:
                continue
            os.environ[var] = str(value).strip()
            found[var] = path.name
    if verbose:
        print(credentials_report(found))
    return found


def _all_key_vars() -> list[str]:
    """Every variable any registered model might read, de-duplicated in order."""
    return list(dict.fromkeys(v for s in MODELS.values() for v in s.key_env))


def _read_json_keys(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {str(k): str(v) for k, v in
            json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).items()}


def _read_dotenv(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        name, _, value = line.partition("=")
        out[name.strip()] = value.strip().strip("'\"")
    return out


def save_credentials(**keys: str) -> Path:
    """Write keys to the gitignored :data:`KEY_FILE` so they are set once.

    Merges rather than replaces, so saving one provider's key does not drop
    another's. On POSIX the file is chmod 600; on Windows it inherits the
    directory's ACL, which is why the directory is created here rather than by
    hand.
    """
    import os
    import stat

    SECRETS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    current = _read_json_keys(KEY_FILE) if KEY_FILE.exists() else {}
    current.update({k: v for k, v in keys.items() if v})
    KEY_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(current, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        os.chmod(KEY_FILE, stat.S_IRUSR | stat.S_IWUSR)
    except OSError:
        pass
    for name, value in keys.items():
        if value:
            os.environ[name] = value
    return KEY_FILE


def mask(value: str) -> str:
    """``sk-ant-api03-abc…xyz`` -> ``sk-ant…3f2a`` — enough to tell two keys apart."""
    value = str(value or "")
    if len(value) < 12:
        return "set" if value else "unset"
    return f"{value[:6]}…{value[-4:]}"


def credentials_report(found: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """Which providers can run, which cannot, and why — before anything is spent."""
    import os

    found = found if found is not None else {}
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_pages v{__version__} — credentials", ""]
    for var in _all_key_vars():
        value = os.environ.get(var, "")
        users = sorted(s.key for s in MODELS.values() if var in s.key_env)
        source = found.get(var, "environment" if value else "")
        lines.append(f"  {var:20s} {mask(value):16s} "
                     f"{('from ' + source) if source else 'MISSING':22s} "
                     f"{', '.join(users)}")
    ready, blocked = [], []
    for spec in MODELS.values():
        (ready if any(os.environ.get(v) for v in spec.key_env)
         else blocked).append(spec.key)
    lines += ["", f"  ready:   {', '.join(sorted(ready)) or 'none'}"]
    if blocked:
        lines.append(f"  blocked: {', '.join(sorted(blocked))}")
    lines += ["",
              f"  Keys are read from the environment, then {KEY_FILE.name}, then "
              f"{DOTENV.name}.",
              "  Both files are gitignored. Never paste a key into a notebook "
              "cell: notebooks",
              "  are tracked, and a key in git history is removed by rewriting "
              "history, not by",
              "  deleting the line."]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def check_credentials(config: "RunConfig") -> list[str]:
    """The models this config selects that have no key. Empty means go.

    Called before a batch is built rather than when the first call is made: a
    970-page job that fails to authenticate on request one has still cost the
    time it took to render 970 pages.
    """
    import os

    return [spec.key for spec in config.specs
            if not any(os.environ.get(v) for v in spec.key_env)]

def sweep_variant(base: str, **overrides) -> str:
    """Register a one-off variant of a model and return its key.

    A sweep has to vary one setting and hold everything else fixed, and the
    settings that matter here live on the :data:`MODELS` spec rather than on
    :class:`RunConfig` — temperature above all. Registering the variant as its
    own key means the existing machinery does the rest for free: it gets its own
    ``custom_id``, its own raw files, its own ledger rows and its own row in the
    score table, so two temperatures are compared exactly the way two models are.

        hot = sweep_variant("gemini-3.8-flash", temperature=1.0)   # -> "gemini-3.8-flash@temperature=1.0"

    Variants are deliberately not persisted: they exist for the session that
    declares them, so a sweep cannot quietly become part of the registry and get
    re-run later by something that did not ask for it.
    """
    if base not in MODELS:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown base model {base!r}")
    tag = ",".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(overrides.items()))
    key = f"{base}@{tag}"
    MODELS[key] = replace(MODELS[base], key=key, **overrides)
    return key


#: Output tokens per page, for the **pre-flight estimate only**.
#:
#: Was 7,500, reasoned from the calibration line counts. **Measured on the
#: 2026-09-08 pilot it is 10,200** — and the two readers are nowhere near each
#: other: Gemini 3.8 Flash averaged **13,174** and Haiku 4.5 **7,289** on the same
#: five pages. So the reasoned figure was right for one model and 76 % low for the
#: other, which is the whole argument for pricing a volume run off
#: :func:`project` rather than off this constant. It exists so an estimate is
#: never silently missing the term that dominates the bill.
OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_PAGE = 10_200

#: Fallback for the fixed per-call prefix — system prompt, symbol list, worked
#: example, atlas image — used only when the real prompt cannot be built (no
#: abbreviation table on disk). :func:`prompt_tokens` measures it instead, which
#: matters because the 0449 worked example is 22 KB on its own.
PROMPT_TOKENS_PER_CALL = 5_000


def prompt_tokens(spec: ModelSpec, edition: str = "cz", atlas: bool = True,
                  fewshot: bool = True, source: str = "gold",
                  entries: int = 0, indent: int = 0) -> int:
    """The fixed prefix, measured rather than assumed.

    Four chars to the token is a crude conversion and is not trying to be more —
    the point is that the *worked example* is 22 KB of Markdown, so a hardcoded
    5,000 understates the prefix by more than the prefix itself. The pilot's real
    usage overrides this within the hour.
    """
    try:
        abbreviations = load_abbreviations()
    except Exception:                                   # noqa: BLE001
        return PROMPT_TOKENS_PER_CALL
    text = build_page_system(abbreviations, edition, atlas=atlas,
                             tiled=spec.image_rule.tiles)
    if fewshot:
        shot = (fewshot_from_gold(entries=entries, indent=indent)
                if source == "gold" else "")
        text += shot or load_fewshot()
    total = math.ceil(len(text) / 4)
    if atlas and ATLAS_PNG.exists():
        try:
            from PIL import Image                       # noqa: PLC0415
            with Image.open(ATLAS_PNG) as plate:
                total += tile_tokens(plate.width, plate.height, spec.image_rule)
        except Exception:                               # noqa: BLE001
            pass
    return total


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Run configuration
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

MODES = ("pilot", "full")
TRANSPORTS = ("batch", "sync")
EDITIONS = ("cz", "de")

#: The views. Two views of one page are two votes, and the bake-off's one hard
#: finding about certainty is that **agreement between passes separates and
#: self-reported confidence does not** — every scored pictogram claim in all 23 v1
#: passes came back ``confidence=high``, one bucket, zero variance, at precision
#: 0.73. So a second geometry is not a luxury; it is the only certainty signal
#: this design has.
#:
#: They must differ in what the model *sees*. The v1 rig was deterministic —
#: ``base`` and ``again`` came back byte-identical, noise floor 0.000 — so
#: re-asking the same model the same way returns the same answer, and a "second
#: pass" that happens to produce the same images is not a second opinion, it is
#: the same opinion billed twice.
#:
#: Measured on the 2026-09-08 pilot, **the view matters more than the model**:
#: Gemini 3.8 Flash scored ``entry_exact`` 0.617 on ``bands`` against 0.277 on
#: ``native`` — same model, same page, same prompt. So the variants cut *finer*
#: on the register's own structure rather than trying other sizes of one framing.
#:
#: ``native``     the page whole at full resolution (Gemini) or ten tiles (Anthropic)
#: ``bands``      the three printed documents — table / apparatus / legend
#: ``columns``    bands, with the apparatus split on its printed column rule
#: ``bandsfrac``  bands at FIXED fractions of the page (0.56 / 0.90) instead of
#:                on the printed rules. Not a fallback — a control. The
#:                2026-09-08 run scored entry_exact 0.660 on ``bands`` while a
#:                coordinate bug was silently using these fractions, and 0.340
#:                once the bug was fixed and the real rules were used. The
#:                fraction cut lands *inside* the table, so the apparatus image
#:                carries the last few table rows — and therefore the
#:                municipality numbers the apparatus keys refer to. If that is
#:                why it won, then cutting on the printed rule is the wrong
#:                objective and overlap into the table is a feature.
#: ``halfbands``  bands, each cut in half with an overlap
GEOMETRIES = ("native", "bands", "bandsfrac", "columns", "halfbands")

#: What a pilot runs when nothing is named: the winner plus the variant closest
#: to it that still changes what the model sees.
DEFAULT_GEOMETRIES = ("bands", "columns")


@dataclass
class RunConfig:
    """What to run. Every field has a default; nothing below this needs editing.

    ``mode`` is not a page count with a nicer name. A *pilot* measures tokens,
    cost and accuracy on the five purposive pages and then **projects** the full
    run from what it measured; a *full* run is authorised by that projection. The
    grading steps are identical in both, which is the point — the pilot produces
    the same numbers the volume run will, on five pages, for about a dollar.
    """

    models: Sequence[str] = ("gemini-3.8-flash",)
    mode: str = "pilot"
    transport: str = "batch"
    editions: Sequence[str] = ("cz",)
    geometries: Sequence[str] = GEOMETRIES
    pages: Sequence[int] | None = None      # None -> the mode decides
    fewshot: bool = True
    #: "gold"    a hand-read page rendered as the exact target JSON, built by
    #:           code from the transcription (correct by construction).
    #: "example" the short hand-authored extract — smaller, and the fallback
    #:           when no gold sheet is on disk.
    fewshot_source: str = "gold"
    #: 0 renders the WHOLE gold page (~6.1k tokens compact): it demonstrates how
    #: much a page yields, which is the direct answer to under-reading — the
    #: dominant failure of every reader but Gemini. A positive N bounds it to the
    #: first N municipalities (~2.9k at N=3). ~$2.50 separates them over the full
    #: CZ+DE run, so this is a question for measurement, not for budget.
    fewshot_entries: int = 0
    #: Compact JSON in the example. Pretty-printing costs 25% more tokens and
    #: teaches the model nothing it does not already get from the schema.
    fewshot_indent: int = 0
    atlas: bool = True
    out_dir: Path = DEFAULT_OUT
    run_id: str = ""

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        unknown = [m for m in self.models if m not in MODELS]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unknown model(s) {unknown}; registry has {sorted(MODELS)}")
        if not self.models:
            raise ValueError("models is empty — nothing to run")
        for name, value, allowed in (("mode", self.mode, MODES),
                                     ("transport", self.transport, TRANSPORTS),
                                     ("editions", tuple(self.editions), EDITIONS)):
            bad = ([value] if isinstance(value, str) else list(value))
            bad = [v for v in bad if v not in allowed]
            if bad:
                raise ValueError(f"{name}: {bad} not in {allowed}")
        bad_geom = [g for g in self.geometries if g not in GEOMETRIES]
        if bad_geom:
            raise ValueError(f"geometries: {bad_geom} not in {GEOMETRIES}")
        if not self.geometries:
            raise ValueError("geometries is empty — a pass needs a view")
        self.out_dir = Path(self.out_dir)
        if not self.run_id:
            self.run_id = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")

    # -- derived ---------------------------------------------------------- #

    @property
    def specs(self) -> list[ModelSpec]:
        return [MODELS[m] for m in self.models]

    def pages_for(self, edition: str) -> list[int]:
        """The scans this run reads in one edition.

        A Czech pilot reads the purposive five: the only pages with a hand
        transcription to grade against, and outside the drawn sample, so reading
        them costs the certification interval nothing.

        **The German volume gets no default, in either mode**, and this is the
        important part. The two volumes paginate differently and each orders an
        okres's municipalities alphabetically *in its own language*, so there is
        no scan-to-scan correspondence — German scan 118 is not the German
        printing of Czech scan 118, it is an unrelated page. Returning the Czech
        numbers here would read five arbitrary German pages and hand the CZ/DE
        reconciliation two unrelated sets to compare; it would report near-zero
        overlap, and that would look like the *join* failing rather than the page
        selection being wrong. A fabricated finding is worse than a crash, so
        this raises.

        The register itself refuses the same way one level down —
        ``lexikon_1910_de`` matches municipalities by name within an okres and
        declines a tie rather than breaking it on lookup order — and for the same
        reason: on this source a plausible wrong answer is indistinguishable from
        a right one.

        Pass ``pages=[…]`` explicitly, or use :func:`de_pages_for_okres` to find
        the German pages covering a district.
        """
        de_only = tuple(self.editions) == ("de",)
        if self.pages is not None and (edition == "cz" or de_only):
            return list(self.pages)

        if edition == "de":
            # Derived from the built map, never assumed. The Czech pages this run
            # reads are looked up in `lexikon_1910_de_page_map.csv`, which pairs
            # them by the German municipality names the Czech volume itself
            # prints — so the pairing carries its own evidence, and a row whose
            # verdict is not `matched` contributes nothing.
            cz_pages = (list(self.pages) if self.pages is not None
                        else list(PURPOSIVE_PAGES) if self.mode == "pilot"
                        else list(range(CZ_FIRST_SCAN, CZ_LAST_SCAN + 1)))
            pages = de_pages_for_cz(cz_pages, verbose=False)
            if not pages:
                raise ValueError(
                    "the DE page map covers none of this run's Czech pages with "
                    f"verdict in {DE_MAP_ACCEPT}. Check "
                    f"{DE_PAGE_MAP.name}, widen `accept`, or pass explicit "
                    "pages. There is no CZ->DE scan correspondence to fall back "
                    "on — the volumes paginate differently and each alphabetises "
                    "in its own language.")
            return pages

        if self.mode == "pilot":
            return list(PURPOSIVE_PAGES)
        return list(range(CZ_FIRST_SCAN, CZ_LAST_SCAN + 1))

    def page_reads(self) -> int:
        """Calls at one call per (page, geometry, model)."""
        per_model = sum(len(self.pages_for(e)) for e in self.editions) \
            * len(self.geometries)
        return per_model * len(self.models)

    def rate(self, spec: ModelSpec) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """USD per million in/out, after the batch discount if one applies."""
        factor = spec.batch_discount if self.transport == "batch" else 1.0
        return spec.price_in * factor, spec.price_out * factor

    def paths(self) -> dict[str, Path]:
        base = self.out_dir
        return {
            "base": base,
            "raw": base / "raw" / self.run_id,
            "jobs": base / "jobs",
            "ledger": base / "cost_ledger.csv",
            "claims": base / "claims",
            "reports": base / "reports",
        }


#: What each switch means, in one line each. Kept beside the class rather than
#: only in the notebook so a config printed from a script explains itself too.
CONFIG_HELP: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {

def config_report(config: "RunConfig", help: bool = True) -> str:
    """What this run will do, in plain terms, before it does it."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_pages v{__version__} — run configuration", "",
             f"  run_id      {config.run_id}", ""]
    values = {
        "models": ", ".join(config.models),
        "mode": config.mode,
        "transport": config.transport,
        "editions": ", ".join(config.editions),
        "geometries": ", ".join(config.geometries),
        "pages": ("mode decides" if config.pages is None
                  else f"{len(config.pages)} explicit"),
        "fewshot": f"{config.fewshot} (scan {FEWSHOT_PAGE:04d})",
        "atlas": str(config.atlas),
    }
    for name, value in values.items():
        summary = CONFIG_HELP[name][0]
        lines.append(f"  {name:11s} {str(value):34s} {summary}")
        if help:
            for chunk in _wrap(CONFIG_HELP[name][1], 74):
                lines.append(f"  {'':11s} {chunk}")
            lines.append("")

    pages = {e: len(config.pages_for(e)) for e in config.editions}
    lines += [
        "  ---------------------------------------------------------------",
        f"  pages       {sum(pages.values())}  "
        f"({', '.join(f'{e}: {n}' for e, n in pages.items())})",
        f"  votes/page  {len(config.models) * len(config.geometries)}  "
        f"({len(config.models)} model(s) x {len(config.geometries)} geometry(ies))",
        f"  page reads  {config.page_reads()}  = API calls this run",
    ]
    missing = check_credentials(config)
    lines.append(f"  credentials {'OK' if not missing else 'MISSING for ' + ', '.join(missing)}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _wrap(text: str, width: int) -> list[str]:
    import textwrap
    return textwrap.wrap(text, width) or [""]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Tiling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tile:
    """One image sent to the model, and where on the page it came from."""

    tile_id: str
    box: tuple[int, int, int, int]      # left, top, right, bottom, page pixels
    scale: float                        # 1.0 = native; < 1 = deliberately shrunk
    role: str = "tile"                  # "tile" | "thumbnail"


#: Vertical overlap between stacked tiles, in page pixels. An entry's printed line
#: is 44 px tall and the apparatus sets several to a centimetre, so a cut that
#: lands mid-line loses the line from both tiles unless they overlap. 64 px is
#: comfortably more than one line and costs ~8 % in tokens.
TILE_OVERLAP = 64


def plan_tiles(width: int, height: int, rule: ImageRule,
               cuts: Sequence[int] = (), overlap: int = TILE_OVERLAP,
               thumbnail: bool = True) -> list[Tile]:
    """Cut a page into images the provider will not downscale.

    Returns the thumbnail first when one is asked for. It is there for *layout*:
    the model needs to see that the page is a table above two columns above a
    legend before it is handed a strip of one of them, and a strip alone reads as
    a page with no context. It is deliberately the only downscaled image in the
    call.

    ``cuts`` are preferred row boundaries in page pixels — the printed rules,
    where the ALTO gives them, so a tile edge lands in white space rather than
    through an entry. The nearest cut within half a tile of the ideal position
    wins; where there is none, the ideal position is used and the overlap covers
    it.

    A rule that does not tile returns the page whole (plus no thumbnail — the
    whole page *is* the context), which is the Gemini path.
    """
    if not rule.tiles:
        return [Tile("whole", (0, 0, width, height), 1.0, "page")]

    cols = max(1, math.ceil(width / rule.max_edge))
    tile_w = math.ceil(width / cols)
    # Height is bounded by BOTH thresholds. Taking the min matters: on this page
    # the pixel budget binds well before the long edge does (1357 x 847 is 1.15
    # Mpx while the edge limit would allow 1568), and using max_edge alone would
    # hand the provider an image it silently shrinks — the exact failure this
    # whole module exists to avoid.
    tile_h = min(rule.max_edge, max(1, rule.max_px // max(tile_w, 1)))
    rows = max(1, math.ceil(height / tile_h))

    tiles: list[Tile] = []
    if thumbnail:
        tiles.append(Tile("thumb", (0, 0, width, height),
                          _fit_scale(width, height, rule), "thumbnail"))
    for r in range(rows):
        ideal_top = r * tile_h
        top = max(0, _snap(ideal_top, cuts, tile_h // 2) - (overlap if r else 0))
        bottom = min(height, top + tile_h + (overlap if r else 0))
        if bottom <= top:
            continue
        for c in range(cols):
            left = c * tile_w
            right = min(width, left + tile_w)
            tiles.append(Tile(f"r{r}c{c}", (left, top, right, bottom), 1.0))
        if bottom >= height:
            break
    return tiles


def _snap(position: int, cuts: Sequence[int], tolerance: int) -> int:
    """The nearest printed rule to ``position``, if one is close enough."""
    if not cuts:
        return position
    nearest = min(cuts, key=lambda c: abs(c - position))
    return nearest if abs(nearest - position) <= tolerance else position


def _fit_scale(width: int, height: int, rule: ImageRule) -> float:
    """How far the provider would shrink this image — 1.0 if it would not."""
    if not rule.tiles or not rule.max_edge:
        return 1.0
    by_edge = rule.max_edge / max(width, height)
    by_area = math.sqrt(rule.max_px / (width * height)) if rule.max_px else 1.0
    return min(1.0, by_edge, by_area)


def tile_tokens(width: int, height: int, rule: ImageRule,
                tiles: Sequence[Tile] | None = None) -> int:
    """Image tokens for one page under one rule — the estimate's input term."""
    tiles = tiles if tiles is not None else plan_tiles(width, height, rule)
    total = 0
    for tile in tiles:
        left, top, right, bottom = tile.box
        w, h = int((right - left) * tile.scale), int((bottom - top) * tile.scale)
        total += rule.tokens(max(w, 1), max(h, 1))
    return total


def cut_tiles(image, tiles: Sequence[Tile]) -> list[tuple[Any, Tile]]:
    """Apply a tile plan to a rendered page. Pillow in, Pillow out."""
    out = []
    for tile in tiles:
        crop = image.crop(tile.box)
        if tile.scale < 1.0:
            crop = crop.resize((max(1, int(crop.width * tile.scale)),
                                max(1, int(crop.height * tile.scale))))
        out.append((crop, tile))
    return out


def rule_cuts(page) -> list[int]:
    """Printed-rule row positions on an ALTO page, for :func:`plan_tiles`.

    Reads ``AltoPage.horizontals`` — the same rule set the grid fitter uses — so a
    tile boundary and a column boundary come from one source. Returns an empty
    list where the ALTO gives nothing (the German volume; Czech pages whose rules
    were not found), and the caller then falls back to the ideal cut plus the
    overlap. **No geometry is invented**: a missing rule means a slightly worse cut
    position, never a guessed one.
    """
    if page is None:
        return []
    cuts: set[int] = set()
    try:
        from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910 as lx
        cuts.update(lx.body_band(page))
    except Exception:                                   # noqa: BLE001
        pass
    for rule in getattr(page, "horizontals", None) or []:
        try:
            cuts.add(int(rule["VPOS"]) + int(rule["HEIGHT"]))
        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
    return sorted(c for c in cuts if c > 0)


#: Fallback band edges as a share of page height, used only where the ALTO gives
#: no rules — the German volume, and Czech pages whose divider was not found.
#: Crude, and deliberately so: a different framing is still a different framing,
#: and the alternative is a second pass identical to the first, which informs
#: nothing at all.
_FALLBACK_BANDS = (0.0, 0.56, 0.90, 1.0)


def page_bands(height: int, page=None) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """The three stacked documents of one page, as ``(top, bottom)`` pairs.

    ``lx.body_band`` gives the table's own top and bottom from the printed frame.
    The apparatus runs from there to the footer divider — the **last** long
    horizontal rule that sits below the table, which is what separates the
    two-column part from the legend. Everything after it is the legend.

    Taken this way rather than by indexing a sorted list of every rule on the
    page: a page carries dozens of horizontals, and "the second one" is a position
    in a list, not a feature of the print.
    """
    if page is not None:
        try:
            from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910 as lx
            _top, body_bottom = lx.body_band(page)
            below = sorted(int(r["VPOS"]) + int(r["HEIGHT"])
                           for r in (getattr(page, "horizontals", None) or [])
                           if int(r["VPOS"]) > body_bottom + 100)
            divider = below[-1] if below else int(height * 0.90)
            edges = [0, int(body_bottom), int(divider), height]
            if all(b - a >= 40 for a, b in zip(edges, edges[1:])):
                return list(zip(edges, edges[1:]))
        except Exception:                               # noqa: BLE001
            pass
    edges = [int(height * f) for f in _FALLBACK_BANDS]
    return list(zip(edges, edges[1:]))


def plan_bands(width: int, height: int, rule: ImageRule,
               bands: Sequence[tuple[int, int]] = (),
               column_split: int = 0, split_band: int = 1) -> list[Tile]:
    """The page cut on its own printed divisions — the second view.

    The register prints three stacked documents (*Návod* p. VI) and this cuts on
    them: the table, the two-column apparatus, the legend below the rule. That is
    a genuinely different **framing** from :func:`plan_tiles`, not a different
    size of the same one, which is what makes it worth a second vote — the v1 rig
    was deterministic, so a second pass only informs when the model sees something
    different.

    Each band is subdivided further if the provider would otherwise downscale it,
    so nothing here costs resolution.
    """
    bands = list(bands) or page_bands(height)
    tiles: list[Tile] = []
    for i, (top, bottom) in enumerate(bands):
        if bottom - top < 40:
            continue
        # The apparatus is a two-column FLOW, not a two-part layout: text runs
        # down the left column and continues at the top of the right. Handed both
        # in one image a reader transcribes across the divider line by line and
        # interleaves two districts. Splitting on the printed rule keeps reading
        # order, and each half is passed separately so the order is the file
        # order rather than something the model has to infer.
        spans = ([(0, column_split), (column_split, width)]
                 if column_split and i == split_band else [(0, width)])
        for j, (x0, x1) in enumerate(spans):
            for sub in plan_tiles(x1 - x0, bottom - top, rule, cuts=(),
                                  thumbnail=False):
                left, s_top, right, s_bottom = sub.box
                tiles.append(Tile(
                    f"b{i}{'lr'[j] if len(spans) > 1 else ''}{sub.tile_id}",
                    (x0 + left, top + s_top, x0 + right,
                     min(height, top + s_bottom)), sub.scale))
    return tiles


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The page schema
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#
# Five arrays, mirroring the register's own division of a page (Návod p. VI: the
# tabular part, the two-column part, the part below the rule) plus the asterisk
# footnotes, which nobody has ever read.
#
# JSON on the wire and nothing else. A model asked for CSV puts a comma inside
# `Kbelnice, Kbelnitz` or a newline inside a footnote and every following field
# shifts, silently and without a grammatical trace — the failure shape that
# `check_atlas_parties.py` and `check_unterricht_transcription.py` exist to catch
# in hand transcription. The schema is enforced by the provider, not requested in
# prose, which is also what stops a model inventing a symbol token.

_TABLE_COLUMNS = [
    "seq", "name", "area_ha", "houses", "pop_total", "pop_male", "pop_female",
    "conf_catholic", "conf_evangelical", "conf_israelite", "conf_other",
    "lang_german", "lang_czech", "lang_other", "foreigners",
    "post_key", "station_note",
]


def _obj(properties: dict, required: Sequence[str]) -> dict:
    return {"type": "object", "properties": properties,
            "required": list(required), "additionalProperties": False}


def _s(description: str) -> dict:
    """A string field that says what it is.

    Every field carried a bare ``{"type": "string"}`` until 2026-09-09, and the
    2026-09-08 pilot is what that cost. The register keys an apparatus entry
    ``1, 2)`` — municipality 1, settlement 2 — and the rule was stated once, in
    prose, in the middle of a long page description. Gemini inferred it. Haiku
    took the *second* number as the municipality on every entry it read, so its
    symbols were fine (precision 0.70) and filed against the wrong place, which
    put ``entry_exact`` at 0.103 against Gemini's 0.617.

    A description sits next to the field while the model fills it, and both
    providers honour it. That is where a per-field rule belongs — not in a
    paragraph the model read once, four thousand tokens earlier.
    """
    return {"type": "string", "description": description}


#: Stated in the schema, in the prompt, and once more as a worked parse, because
#: this single convention decides whether every symbol on the page lands on the
#: right municipality or one row off.
_KEY_RULE = ("The apparatus keys each entry with TWO numbers printed as "
             "'m, n)'. The FIRST is the municipality's running number in the "
             "table above; the SECOND is the settlement's number within that "
             "municipality. '1, 2)' is municipality 1, settlement 2 — NOT "
             "municipality 2. '17, —)' is municipality 17 taken as a whole: "
             "settlement_seq is '0'.")


def _arr(items: dict) -> dict:
    return {"type": "array", "items": items}


_TABLE_HELP = {
    "seq": "Running number in the leftmost narrow column, as printed.",
    "name": "Place name as printed, usually 'Czech, German'. Keep both.",
    "area_ha": "Area in hectares. Printed ONLY on the municipality line — "
               "leave '' on settlement lines.",
    "post_key": "Postal delivery district footnote key, e.g. '13)'.",
    "station_note": "Nearest station and walking distance, e.g. '10) 2 1/4'.",
}

PAGE_SCHEMA: dict = _obj({
    "running_head": _s("The line above the table: 'political okres: court "
                       "district.' e.g. 'Chomútov: Chomútov, Jirkov.'"),
    "table": _arr(_obj(
        {c: _s(_TABLE_HELP.get(c, f"Column '{c}', as printed. '' if the cell is "
                                  "empty or holds the centred nil dot."))
         for c in _TABLE_COLUMNS}, _TABLE_COLUMNS)),
    "parts": _arr(_obj({
        "court": _s("Soudní okres named in this section's heading."),
        "muni_seq": _s("FIRST number of the 'm, n)' key. " + _KEY_RULE),
        "settlement_seq": _s("SECOND number of the 'm, n)' key, or '0' for a "
                             "dash. " + _KEY_RULE),
        "part_name": _s("Name of the named part, as printed."),
        "symbols": _arr(_s("One token from the closed list, or [?] / [!].")),
        "houses": _s("Houses figure of the house-population pair."),
        "population": _s("Population figure of the house-population pair."),
    }, ["court", "muni_seq", "settlement_seq", "part_name", "symbols",
        "houses", "population"])),
    "offices": _arr(_obj({
        "court": _s("Soudní okres named in this section's heading."),
        "muni_seq": _s("FIRST number of the 'm, n)' key. " + _KEY_RULE),
        "settlement_seq": _s("SECOND number of the 'm, n)' key, or '0' for a "
                             "dash. " + _KEY_RULE),
        "place_name": _s("Place this entry is about, if the entry names one; "
                         "otherwise ''. Do not copy it from the table."),
        "symbols": _arr(_s("One token from the closed list, or [?] / [!]. "
                           "List each printed mark ONCE, in printed order.")),
        "text": _s("The entry's remaining printed words, WITHOUT the symbol "
                   "tokens — those belong in `symbols` and must not be "
                   "repeated here."),
        "altitude": _s("Altitude if printed, e.g. '314 m'; else ''."),
    }, ["court", "muni_seq", "settlement_seq", "place_name", "symbols",
        "text", "altitude"])),
    "legend": _arr(_obj({
        "key": _s("The footnote number the table's last two columns point at."),
        "kind": _s("'post' or 'rail', whichever this key names."),
        "text": _s("The legend entry as printed."),
    }, ["key", "kind", "text"])),
    "footnotes": _arr(_obj({
        "marker": _s("The printed marker, e.g. '*)' or '**)'."),
        "text": _s("The footnote text as printed."),
    }, ["marker", "text"])),
}, ["running_head", "table", "parts", "offices", "legend", "footnotes"])


def to_gemini_schema(schema: dict) -> dict:
    """JSON Schema -> the OpenAPI subset ``response_schema`` accepts.

    One schema definition, converted, rather than two hand-written ones. Two
    definitions of the same shape drift on the first edit and the drift is silent:
    one provider starts returning a field the other does not, and the comparison
    between them — the entire reason both are being run — quietly stops being
    like-for-like.

    ``additionalProperties`` is dropped because the subset rejects it, and
    ``propertyOrdering`` is added because Gemini honours it and a stable field
    order makes two runs diffable.
    """
    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
        return schema
    out: dict = {}
    for key, value in schema.items():
        if key == "additionalProperties":
            continue
        if key == "type":
            out["type"] = str(value).upper()
        elif key == "properties":
            out["properties"] = {k: to_gemini_schema(v) for k, v in value.items()}
            out["propertyOrdering"] = list(value)
        elif key == "items":
            out["items"] = to_gemini_schema(value)
        else:
            out[key] = value
    return out


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The prompt
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

_TABLE_SPEC = """\
1  seq              the running number in the leftmost narrow column
2  name             place name, often "Czech, German" together, sometimes with
                    printed symbols and bracketed figures after it
3  area_ha          area in hectares — printed ONLY on the municipality line
4  houses           number of houses
5  pop_total        present population, together
6  pop_male         present population, male
7  pop_female       present population, female
8  conf_catholic    Roman Catholic
9  conf_evangelical Evangelical
10 conf_israelite   Israelite
11 conf_other       other or no confession
12 lang_german      nationals by language of daily use: German
13 lang_czech       nationals by language of daily use: Czech-Moravian-Slovak
14 lang_other       nationals by language of daily use: other
15 foreigners       foreign nationals
16 post_key         postal delivery district — a footnote key such as "13)"
17 station_note     nearest railway station and walking distance, e.g. "10) 2 1/4"
"""

_HEAD = """\
You are transcribing one page of the 1910 Austrian census place register — \
{title} — printed in Vienna, {year}, in {language}.

The page holds THREE stacked documents, and the register says so itself (Návod \
p. VI). Read all of them, plus any footnotes.

1. TABELÁRNÍ ČÁST — the table. 17 columns between printed vertical rules, in this
   left-to-right order:

{table_spec}
   A bold municipality row carries the area in hectares; the settlement rows
   beneath it do not. That is what marks where one block ends and the next begins.

2. DVOUSLOUPCOVÁ ČÁST — two columns of small type beneath the table. It is a
   FLOW, not a two-part layout: text runs down the left column and continues at
   the top of the right. Two kinds of section alternate, each under its own
   heading:
     "Části osad v soudním okresu X:"  names the parts each settlement consists
       of, each with a topographic symbol and a houses—population pair.
     "Úřady, ústavy a t. d. v soudním okresu X:"  lists what each place HAD.
   HOW AN ENTRY IS KEYED — get this right before anything else, because every
   symbol on the page hangs on it:
     Each entry opens with TWO numbers printed "m, n)".
     m (bold)  = the municipality's running number in the table above.
     n (light) = the settlement's number WITHIN that municipality.
     "1, 2)"  -> muni_seq "1", settlement_seq "2"   (municipality ONE, not two)
     "17, —)" -> muni_seq "17", settlement_seq "0"  (the municipality as a whole)
   The numbers run 1, 1) 1, 2) 1, 3) 2, —) 3, —) — so a rising second number
   under an unchanged first is normal and does NOT mean the municipality changed.

3. JEDNOSLOUPCOVÁ ČÁST POD ČAROU — the full-width legend below the rule: the
   postal delivery districts and railway stations that the table's last two
   columns point at by number.

4. Any footnotes marked with *) or **).
"""

_SYMBOL_RULES = """\

SYMBOLS. Most of what section 2 records is printed as PICTOGRAMS, not words. You
may name a symbol ONLY with a token from this closed list:

{tokens}

Two escapes, and both are data rather than failure:
  {unknown}  printed but you cannot tell which symbol it is
  [!]  clearly printed, clearly a symbol, and not on the list above

Never invent a token. A plausible wrong token resolves cleanly through the
decoder downstream and becomes an institution that was never printed, which is
strictly worse than an honest {unknown}.
"""

_RESTRAINT = """\

WHAT TO RETURN, AND WHAT NOT TO.
- Transcribe exactly what is printed. Do not correct, complete, infer, or compute
  any value from any other value. The figures are checked against each other
  later, and a reading that has been made to add up measures nothing.
- If a figure is genuinely illegible, return "?" — never a plausible number.
- A centred dot or dash is the printed NIL marker and means a true zero. Return
  "." for it. Return "" only for a cell where nothing is printed at all. These are
  different facts — no Jewish inhabitants is not the same as no figure given — and
  collapsing them loses one of them permanently. Never write "0" for either.
- Return figures as digit strings with no thousands separators.
- Long place names wrap onto a second printed line; join them into one entry.
- Report ONLY what you can see printed. Do not list a symbol because a place of
  this kind would usually have one. Under-reporting is recoverable; a confident
  invention is not.
"""

_TILE_NOTE = """\

You are being shown the page as several overlapping images: first a small view of
the whole page for layout, then strips at full resolution in reading order. The
strips overlap, so an entry may appear twice — report it ONCE. Ignore any row cut
off at the very top or bottom edge of a strip if it appears whole in another.
"""

_ATLAS_NOTE = """\

The final image is the volume's own Výklad značek plate: every symbol, drawn, with
its name. Match against it. The plate prints the symbols at display size while the
entries print the same designs at roughly 0.45x, so compare the SHAPE, not the size.
"""

_EDITIONS = {
    "cz": {"title": "Podrobný seznam míst v Čechách", "year": "1916",
           "language": "Czech", "lang_code": "cs"},
    "de": {"title": "Spezialortsrepertorium von Böhmen", "year": "1915",
           "language": "German", "lang_code": "de"},
}


def build_page_system(abbreviations, edition: str = "cz", atlas: bool = True,
                      tiled: bool = True) -> str:
    """The whole-page prompt, with the token list read off the curated table.

    Built rather than written out, for the reason v1 already established: a token
    list typed into a prompt and a token table read by the decoder drift apart on
    the first edit, and the failure is silent in the worst direction — the model
    emits a token nobody can resolve and the symbol is lost exactly as if it had
    never been read. :func:`~utils.lexikon_1910.lexikon_1910_vision.pictograms` is the
    single definition.

    The prompt leans on *restraint* because that is what the bake-off measured:
    the union of 23 passes asserted 1,280 claims for 280 true ones. These readers
    fail by over-asserting, not by under-seeing, so the instruction that earns its
    tokens is the one telling them to stop.
    """
    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv

    meta = _EDITIONS.get(edition)
    if meta is None:
        raise ValueError(f"edition must be one of {sorted(_EDITIONS)}, got {edition!r}")

    tokens = "\n".join(
        f"  {a.code:22s} {a.english or a.expansion}"
        for a in lxv.pictograms(abbreviations))
    prompt = _HEAD.format(table_spec=_TABLE_SPEC, **{
        k: meta[k] for k in ("title", "year", "language")})
    prompt += _SYMBOL_RULES.format(tokens=tokens, unknown=lxv.UNKNOWN_TOKEN)
    prompt += _RESTRAINT
    if tiled:
        prompt += _TILE_NOTE
    if atlas:
        prompt += _ATLAS_NOTE
    return prompt


#: A real printed extract from soudní okres Jičín and the exact JSON it becomes.
#:
#: Replaces the raw gold worksheet, which was 22 KB — about 5,300 tokens on every
#: call — of YAML front matter, image filenames, section headings and HTML
#: comments holding *the text layer's garbage OCR* (``18, —) Ф, Ä ca. 700 m, Ц
#: IV, S, f, doč. 3 Д``). It showed content and restraint and **never once showed
#: the JSON the model has to produce**, which is the one thing a worked example on
#: a schema-constrained task is for. Four hundred tokens of the right shape beat
#: five thousand of the wrong one.
#:
#: The extract is chosen to carry every convention that bit the pilot in four
#: lines: the ``m, n)`` key, the ``m, —)`` whole-municipality dash, an entry that
#: names places *inside* itself, and a symbol list kept out of ``text``.
_WORKED_EXAMPLE = """

WORKED EXAMPLE. This is printed in the offices section of one page:

    17, —) Kartouzy: † 314 m, věznice pro muže s nemocenským odděl., [midwife].
           Valdice: [school] III, [pharmacy], [fire-brigade], [post], [rail-station] 301 m.
    18,  1) [fire-brigade].
           Zebín: † 400 m.

It becomes exactly this — note that 18, 1) is municipality 18 settlement 1, NOT
municipality 1; that a dash makes settlement_seq "0"; that a place named inside
the entry gets its own object; and that no symbol token is repeated in `text`:

    {"court": "Jičín", "muni_seq": "17", "settlement_seq": "0",
     "place_name": "Kartouzy", "symbols": ["[rc-parish]", "[midwife]"],
     "text": "věznice pro muže s nemocenským odděl.", "altitude": "314 m"}
    {"court": "Jičín", "muni_seq": "17", "settlement_seq": "0",
     "place_name": "Valdice",
     "symbols": ["[school]", "[pharmacy]", "[fire-brigade]", "[post]", "[rail-station]"],
     "text": "III, 301 m", "altitude": ""}
    {"court": "Jičín", "muni_seq": "18", "settlement_seq": "1",
     "place_name": "", "symbols": ["[fire-brigade]"], "text": "", "altitude": ""}
    {"court": "Jičín", "muni_seq": "18", "settlement_seq": "1",
     "place_name": "Zebín", "symbols": ["[rc-parish]"], "text": "",
     "altitude": "400 m"}

Do not carry any name, number or symbol from this example onto the page you are
reading now.
"""


def fewshot_from_gold(page: int = FEWSHOT_PAGE, entries: int = 0,
                      indent: int = 1) -> str:
    """A hand-read page, rendered as exactly the JSON the schema asks for.

    Built by code from ``read_transcription_md.read_sheet`` rather than written
    out, and that is the point: a hand-authored example is where an invalid token
    gets in. The first draft of :data:`_WORKED_EXAMPLE` taught ``[rc-church]``
    and ``[rail]``, neither of which exists — inside the example whose whole job
    is to enforce the closed list. An example derived from the gold is correct by
    construction and rebuilds when the transcription is corrected.

    ``entries`` bounds it to the first N municipalities; 0 renders the whole page.
    The choice is a parameter because it is an open question, not a preference:
    a whole page demonstrates **completeness** — that one page yields ~20 table
    rows, ~93 parts and ~30 offices entries — and under-reading is the dominant
    failure of every model but Gemini (Sonnet returned one offices entry on a
    page holding twenty; Haiku returned three parts where the truth was
    sixty-seven). Against that, a long example raises the risk that names and
    numbers get carried onto the page being read. ~7k tokens is about **$2.50
    over the whole CZ+DE run**, so cost does not decide it — measurement does.

    Returns "" when the sheet is not on disk: a missing example is a weaker
    prompt, not a broken run.
    """
    sheet_path = GOLD_DIR / "purposive" / f"{page:04d}.md"
    if not sheet_path.exists():
        return ""
    import importlib.util                               # noqa: PLC0415

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "_rtm", ROOT / "utils" / "lexikon_1910" / "read_transcription_md.py")
    rtm = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys_path_added = str(ROOT / "utils" / "lexikon_1910")
    import sys                                          # noqa: PLC0415
    if sys_path_added not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, sys_path_added)
    spec.loader.exec_module(rtm)

    from utils.lexikon_1910 import lexikon_1910_vision as lxv
    sheet = rtm.read_sheet(sheet_path, lxv.vocabulary(load_abbreviations()))

    keep = None
    if entries:
        seen: list = []
        for row in sheet.get("offices") or []:
            key = (row.get("district"), str(row.get("muni_seq")))
            if key not in seen:
                seen.append(key)
        keep = set(seen[:entries])

    def wanted(row) -> bool:
        return keep is None or (row.get("district"),
                                str(row.get("muni_seq"))) in keep

    # offices arrive one row per SYMBOL; the schema wants one object per entry.
    grouped: dict = {}
    for row in sheet.get("offices") or []:
        if not wanted(row):
            continue
        key = (row.get("district"), str(row.get("muni_seq")),
               str(row.get("settlement_seq") or "0"))
        obj = grouped.setdefault(key, {
            "court": row.get("district", ""), "muni_seq": key[1],
            "settlement_seq": key[2],
            "place_name": (row.get("settlement") or "").replace(
                "(obec as a whole)", ""),
            "symbols": [], "text": "", "altitude": ""})
        if row.get("code"):
            obj["symbols"].append(row["code"])

    payload = {
        "table": [{c: r.get(c, "") for c in _TABLE_COLUMNS}
                  for r in (sheet.get("table") or []) if keep is None
                  or str(r.get("seq")) in {k[1] for k in keep}],
        "parts": [{"court": r.get("district", ""),
                   "muni_seq": str(r.get("muni_seq")),
                   "settlement_seq": str(r.get("settlement_seq") or "0"),
                   "part_name": r.get("part_name", ""),
                   "symbols": [r["topographic"]] if r.get("topographic") else [],
                   "houses": r.get("houses", ""),
                   "population": r.get("population", "")}
                  for r in (sheet.get("parts") or []) if wanted(r)],
        "offices": list(grouped.values()),
        "legend": [{"key": r.get("key", ""), "kind": "",
                    "text": r.get("place", "")}
                   for r in (sheet.get("legend") or [])][: 6 if keep else None],
    }
    body = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False,
                      indent=indent if indent else None,
                      separators=None if indent else (",", ":"))
    scope = (f"the first {entries} municipalities of a" if entries
             else "one whole")
    return (
        f"\n\nWORKED EXAMPLE — {scope} page of this volume, read by hand, in "
        f"exactly the shape you must return.\n\nNote how many rows a page "
        f"yields: read the page to the END of every section rather than stopping "
        f"early. Note that '18, 1)' is municipality 18 settlement 1, that a dash "
        f"gives settlement_seq '0', and that a symbol appears in `symbols` and "
        f"never in `text`.\n\nDo NOT carry any name, number or symbol from this "
        f"example onto the page you are reading now.\n\n" + body + "\n")


def load_fewshot(page: int = FEWSHOT_PAGE) -> str:
    """The worked example: printed text in, target JSON out.

    ``page`` is accepted and ignored, kept so callers that named
    :data:`FEWSHOT_PAGE` still work. The page-shaped example it used to load is
    documented at :data:`_WORKED_EXAMPLE` — it is not merely bigger, it taught
    the wrong thing.

    The contamination rule that chose :data:`FEWSHOT_PAGE` is unchanged and now
    trivially satisfied: this extract is from soudní okres Jičín, which appears
    on no page in :data:`GOLD_SCORED_PAGES`, so nothing here grades a model
    against its own prompt.
    """
    return _WORKED_EXAMPLE


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Usage and the cost ledger
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@dataclass
class Usage:
    """What one call actually cost, as reported by the provider."""

    input: int = 0
    output: int = 0
    cache_read: int = 0
    cache_write: int = 0

    def __add__(self, other: "Usage") -> "Usage":
        return Usage(self.input + other.input, self.output + other.output,
                     self.cache_read + other.cache_read,
                     self.cache_write + other.cache_write)

    def cost(self, rate_in: float, rate_out: float) -> float:
        """Cached reads bill at a tenth, cache writes at 1.25x."""
        return ((self.input + self.cache_read * 0.1 + self.cache_write * 1.25)
                * rate_in + self.output * rate_out) / 1e6


LEDGER_COLUMNS = ["run_id", "custom_id", "edition", "scan", "model", "geometry",
                  "transport", "input", "output", "cache_read", "cache_write",
                  "cost_usd", "seconds", "status"]


def append_ledger(path: Path, rows: Iterable[dict]) -> int:
    """Append to the cost ledger, creating it with a header if absent."""
    rows = list(rows)
    if not rows:
        return 0
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    exists = path.exists()
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=LEDGER_COLUMNS,
                                extrasaction="ignore")
        if not exists:
            writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)
    return len(rows)


def read_ledger(path: Path, run_id: str = "") -> list[dict]:
    if not Path(path).exists():
        return []
    with Path(path).open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    return [r for r in rows if not run_id or r.get("run_id") == run_id]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Estimating, before anything is spent
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def page_size(edition: str = "cz", scan: int = 118,
              width: int | None = None) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """The rendered pixel size of one page, without rendering it.

    Read off the PDF's own page rectangle and the ALTO frame width, so the
    estimate is grounded in the volume rather than in a remembered number. The CZ
    page is 528 x 774 pt; at the 2,714 px ALTO width that is 2,714 x 3,976.
    """
    import fitz

    pdf = CZ_PDF if edition == "cz" else DE_PDF
    with fitz.open(str(pdf)) as doc:
        rect = doc[scan - 1].rect
    target = width or DEFAULT_RENDER_WIDTH
    return target, round(target * rect.height / rect.width)


#: The ALTO frame width the Czech volume renders at, so every ALTO coordinate
#: lands 1:1 on a pixel. The German volume has no ALTO; it is rendered at the same
#: width so the two are compared at the same scale rather than at whatever each
#: scan happened to be cropped to.
DEFAULT_RENDER_WIDTH = 2714


def estimate(config: RunConfig,
             output_tokens: int = OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_PAGE) -> list[dict]:
    """Price the run from the tiler and the registry. **No API calls.**

    One row per (model, geometry). The point is that a volume run is never
    launched un-priced: the numbers here are projections, but they exist before a
    cent is spent and :func:`project` replaces them with measurements as soon as
    the pilot has produced any.
    """
    rows: list[dict] = []
    # One representative page per edition, with its real printed rules, so the
    # estimate's tile count is the one the run will actually produce.
    sample = {e: (page_size(e), alto_page(118) if e == "cz" else None)
              for e in config.editions}
    for spec in config.specs:
        rate_in, rate_out = config.rate(spec)
        prefix = prompt_tokens(spec, atlas=config.atlas, fewshot=config.fewshot,
                               source=config.fewshot_source,
                               entries=config.fewshot_entries,
                               indent=config.fewshot_indent)
        for geometry in config.geometries:
            for edition in config.editions:
                (width, height), page = sample[edition]
                tiles = _tiles_for(width, height, spec, geometry, page)
                img = tile_tokens(width, height, spec.image_rule, tiles)
                per_in = img + prefix
                per_page = (per_in * rate_in + output_tokens * rate_out) / 1e6
                pages = len(config.pages_for(edition))
                full_pages = (CZ_PAGE_COUNT if edition == "cz"
                              else DE_PAGE_COUNT_ESTIMATE)
                rows.append({
                    "model": spec.key, "geometry": geometry, "edition": edition,
                    "page_px": f"{width}x{height}", "tiles": len(tiles),
                    "input_tokens_per_page": per_in,
                    "output_tokens_per_page": output_tokens,
                    "usd_per_page": round(per_page, 5),
                    "pages_this_run": pages,
                    "usd_this_run": round(per_page * pages, 4),
                    "usd_full_edition": round(per_page * full_pages, 2),
                    "transport": config.transport,
                    "rate_in": rate_in, "rate_out": rate_out,
                    "measured": False,
                })
    return rows


def _tiles_for(width: int, height: int, spec: ModelSpec, geometry: str,
               page=None, image=None) -> list[Tile]:
    """The image plan for one geometry, on one provider.

    The single place the views are defined, so the estimator and the request
    builder cannot drift apart on what a "pass" is — which they would the moment
    one of them re-derived the plan itself.

    ``page`` is the ALTO page when there is one. Where there is not, every view
    still works: the tiler falls back to the ideal cut plus overlap, the bands to
    fixed shares, and the column split is simply not made. Nothing here invents a
    coordinate it did not measure.
    """
    if geometry == "native":
        return plan_tiles(width, height, spec.image_rule, rule_cuts(page))

    # `bandsfrac` deliberately ignores the ALTO: passing page=None takes the
    # fixed-fraction path, which is exactly what the 2026-09-08 run was doing by
    # accident. Same call, same prompt, same everything else — only the edges
    # differ, so a difference in score is attributable to the edges.
    bands = page_bands(height, None if geometry == "bandsfrac" else page)
    if geometry == "halfbands":
        bands = [half for band in bands for half in _split_band(band)]

    split = 0
    if geometry == "columns" and len(bands) > 1:
        # The ALTO first where there is one — a rule the engine already found
        # needs no threshold — then the image. The image path is not merely a
        # fallback for the German volume: on the five Czech development pages it
        # reproduces the ALTO's answer exactly on all four that have one, and
        # recovers 0270, where the ALTO reports no divider at all.
        split = apparatus_divider(page, bands[1])
        if not split and image is not None:
            split = detect_divider(image, bands[1])
    return plan_bands(width, height, spec.image_rule, bands,
                      column_split=split, split_band=1)


def _split_band(band: tuple[int, int]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
    """Cut one band in two, with the overlap a printed line needs to survive."""
    top, bottom = band
    if bottom - top < 400:
        return [band]
    middle = (top + bottom) // 2
    return [(top, middle + TILE_OVERLAP), (middle - TILE_OVERLAP, bottom)]


def project(config: RunConfig, ledger: Sequence[dict] | None = None,
            path: Path | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    """Re-price the run from measured usage. This is what authorises a full run.

    Falls back to :func:`estimate` for any (model, geometry) the ledger has not
    seen, and marks each row ``measured`` so the two are never confused in a
    report. An estimate presented as a measurement is how a run gets authorised
    on a number nobody checked.
    """
    rows = read_ledger(path or config.paths()["ledger"], config.run_id) \
        if ledger is None else list(ledger)
    seen: dict[tuple[str, str], list[dict]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        if row.get("status") not in (None, "", "ok"):
            continue
        seen[(row.get("model", ""), row.get("geometry", ""))].append(row)

    out: list[dict] = []
    for row in estimate(config):
        key = (row["model"], row["geometry"])
        calls = seen.get(key)
        if not calls:
            out.append(row)
            continue
        spec = MODELS[row["model"]]
        rate_in, rate_out = config.rate(spec)
        n = len(calls)
        mean_in = sum(int(c.get("input") or 0) for c in calls) / n
        mean_out = sum(int(c.get("output") or 0) for c in calls) / n
        per_page = (mean_in * rate_in + mean_out * rate_out) / 1e6
        full_pages = (CZ_PAGE_COUNT if row["edition"] == "cz"
                      else DE_PAGE_COUNT_ESTIMATE)
        out.append({**row,
                    "input_tokens_per_page": round(mean_in),
                    "output_tokens_per_page": round(mean_out),
                    "usd_per_page": round(per_page, 5),
                    "usd_this_run": round(per_page * row["pages_this_run"], 4),
                    "usd_full_edition": round(per_page * full_pages, 2),
                    "calls_measured": n, "measured": True})
    return out


def estimate_report(rows: Sequence[dict], title: str = "estimate") -> str:
    """Ledger for :func:`estimate` / :func:`project`."""
    lines = [f"lexikon_1910_pages v{__version__} — {title}", ""]
    if not rows:
        return "\n".join(lines + ["  nothing to price"])
    head = (f"  {'model':18s} {'geom':7s} {'ed':3s} {'tiles':>5s} "
            f"{'in/pg':>8s} {'out/pg':>8s} {'$/page':>9s} "
            f"{'$ this run':>11s} {'$ full ed.':>11s}  src")
    lines.append(head)
    lines.append("  " + "-" * (len(head) - 2))
    for r in rows:
        lines.append(
            f"  {r['model']:18s} {r['geometry']:7s} {r['edition']:3s} "
            f"{r['tiles']:5d} {r['input_tokens_per_page']:8,d} "
            f"{r['output_tokens_per_page']:8,d} {r['usd_per_page']:9.5f} "
            f"{r['usd_this_run']:11.2f} {r['usd_full_edition']:11.2f}  "
            f"{'measured' if r.get('measured') else 'estimate'}")
    lines.append("  " + "-" * (len(head) - 2))
    lines.append(f"  {'TOTAL':18s} {'':7s} {'':3s} {'':5s} {'':8s} {'':8s} "
                 f"{'':9s} {sum(r['usd_this_run'] for r in rows):11.2f} "
                 f"{sum(r['usd_full_edition'] for r in rows):11.2f}")
    if any(not r.get("measured") for r in rows):
        lines += ["",
                  "  Estimated rows use "
                  f"{OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_PAGE:,} output tokens/page, which is the",
                  "  largest and least certain term — output is 60–85% of this "
                  "bill. Run the",
                  "  pilot and re-run project() before authorising a volume run."]
    notes = {MODELS[r["model"]].price_note for r in rows if MODELS[r["model"]].price_note}
    for note in sorted(n for n in notes if n):
        lines.append(f"  ! {note}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Adapters
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@dataclass
class PageRequest:
    """One page, one geometry, one model — everything a call needs."""

    custom_id: str
    edition: str
    scan: int
    model: str
    geometry: str
    images: list[tuple[Any, Tile]]      # (PIL image, tile)
    system: str
    atlas: Any | None = None            # PIL image of the Výklad značek plate
    _encoded: list = field(default_factory=list, repr=False)

    def encoded(self) -> list[bytes]:
        """The images as PNG bytes, encoded once and kept.

        Chunking a batch has to know how big each request is, and re-encoding a
        dozen native-resolution tiles per request to find out costs more than
        the submission does.
        """
        if not self._encoded:
            self._encoded = [encode_png(im) for im, _t in self.images]
            if self.atlas is not None:
                self._encoded.append(encode_png(self.atlas))
        return self._encoded

    def payload_bytes(self) -> int:
        """Approximate wire size: base64 inflates by 4/3, plus prompt text."""
        return int(sum(len(b) for b in self.encoded()) * 4 / 3) + len(self.system)


@dataclass
class JobHandle:
    """A submitted batch, persisted so polling survives the session that made it."""

    provider: str
    job_id: str
    model: str
    run_id: str
    custom_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)   # position -> custom_id
    submitted: float = 0.0

    def to_json(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps({"provider": self.provider, "job_id": self.job_id,
                           "model": self.model, "run_id": self.run_id,
                           "custom_ids": self.custom_ids,
                           "submitted": self.submitted}, indent=2)

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "JobHandle":
        return cls(**json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))


class PageReader(Protocol):
    """One interface, two providers.

    Both are written now even though only Google is exercised at first. Writing
    the second later, against an abstraction shaped entirely by the first, is how
    an adapter ends up with a Gemini-shaped hole that Anthropic has to be bent
    into.
    """

    spec: ModelSpec

    def read(self, request: PageRequest) -> tuple[dict, Usage]: ...
    def submit(self, requests: Sequence[PageRequest], run_id: str) -> JobHandle: ...
    def poll(self, job: JobHandle) -> str: ...
    def collect(self, job: JobHandle) -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict | None, Usage, str]]: ...


#: Encode page images as greyscale, losslessly. The scans are grey paper and
#: black type stored as RGB, so the colour channels carry nothing: converting to
#: L takes a rendered page from 15.75 MB to **6.05 MB with no information lost**.
#:
#: That is not cosmetic. A Sonnet request carries a dozen native-resolution tiles
#: plus the atlas, and at RGB that is ~27 MB base64 — so a 52-request batch came
#: to about 1.3 GB against the Message Batches API's **256 MB** ceiling and was
#: refused outright with a 413.
#:
#: JPEG would be smaller again (3.5 MB at q=95), but this volume is read for
#: pictograms that print at ~50x21 px, which is exactly the scale JPEG artefacts
#: live at. A lossy encoding here would trade a measurable accuracy risk for
#: bytes that greyscale already saves, so it stays opt-in and unused by default.
GREYSCALE = True


def encode_png(image, greyscale: bool | None = None) -> bytes:
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    if (GREYSCALE if greyscale is None else greyscale) and image.mode != "L":
        image = image.convert("L")
    image.save(buffer, format="PNG", optimize=False)
    return buffer.getvalue()


class GooglePageReader:
    """Gemini through the native ``google-genai`` SDK.

    Native rather than the OpenAI-compatible shim because the batch API is only on
    the native dialect, and batch is the default transport here.

    **Inline batch requests carry no key.** Google matches ``dest.inlined_responses``
    to the submitted list *by position*; only the JSONL file path accepts an
    explicit ``key``. So the position→``custom_id`` map is persisted on the
    :class:`JobHandle` and the mapping is done here rather than trusted to the
    wire. Getting this wrong would attach every page's reading to a different
    page and still look entirely well-behaved — the same failure shape as joining
    the two editions on their printed numbers.
    """

    def __init__(self, spec: ModelSpec, out_dir: Path = DEFAULT_OUT):
        from google import genai                        # noqa: PLC0415

        self.spec = spec
        self.client = genai.Client()
        self.out_dir = Path(out_dir)
        self._schema = to_gemini_schema(PAGE_SCHEMA)

    # -- request construction --------------------------------------------- #

    def _contents(self, request: PageRequest) -> list[dict]:
        # request.encoded() is cached: chunking already measured this payload,
        # and re-encoding a dozen native-resolution tiles per request costs more
        # than the submission itself.
        blobs = request.encoded()
        parts: list[dict] = [{"text": request.system}]
        for i, (_image, tile) in enumerate(request.images):
            parts.append({"text": f"[{tile.role} {tile.tile_id} "
                                  f"box={tile.box} scale={tile.scale:.2f}]"})
            parts.append({"inline_data": {"mime_type": "image/png",
                                          "data": base64.b64encode(
                                              blobs[i]).decode("ascii")}})
        if request.atlas is not None:
            parts.append({"text": "[Výklad značek — the volume's own symbol plate]"})
            parts.append({"inline_data": {"mime_type": "image/png",
                                          "data": base64.b64encode(
                                              blobs[-1]).decode("ascii")}})
        return [{"role": "user", "parts": parts}]

    def _config(self) -> dict:
        config: dict = {"response_mime_type": "application/json",
                        "response_schema": self._schema,
                        "max_output_tokens": self.spec.max_output_tokens}
        if self.spec.thinking == "off":
            # Thinking bills at the OUTPUT rate and output is 60-85% of this
            # bill, so leaving it to a provider default is the one setting that
            # can make the estimate wrong by a multiple rather than by a margin.
            config["thinking_config"] = {"thinking_budget": 0}
        if self.spec.temperature is not None:
            config["temperature"] = self.spec.temperature
        return config
